title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a preliminary section headed 'Généralités sur coalg. et comodules'. The previous page explains why it is needed: Grothendieck wants to treat divided-power structures, and their 'anti' variants, on coalgebras and comodules in full generality (not only commutative, also anticommutative). For that he first needs the ordinary notions.

Setting. Let k be a ring, S an associative counital k-coalgebra, and C a comodule over S with coaction Δ_C: C → C⊗S. He uses SGA3-style functorial notation:
- V_k(S) is the functor k' ↦ S^{k'} = Hom_{k-mod}(S,k'). It is an algebra-valued functor, with convolution product.
- W(C) is the functor k' ↦ C⊗_k k'.

Step 1: comodule gives module. The comodule structure makes the functor of C a module over the algebra functor V(S). Taking k-points, C becomes an ordinary module over the dual (convolution) algebra S^k = S^* = Hom_k(S,k). For u ∈ S^*, u acts by u_C = (id_C⊗u)∘Δ_C : C → C⊗S → C⊗k ≅ C. The k-module structure is recovered through the unit k → S^*.

Step 2: the converse question. When can the comodule structure be recovered from the S^*-module structure on C alone?
- Functorial answer (his 'NB'): a comodule structure on C is exactly a module structure of W(C) over V(S), i.e. compatible S^{k'}-module structures on C⊗k' for all k'. This is a Yoneda-type statement.
- Pointwise answer: knowing all the u_C is the same as knowing the composite C → C⊗S → ∏_{u∈S^*} C⊗k. So the comodule structure is determined by the module structure as soon as the canonical map C⊗S → ∏_{u∈S^*} C (equivalently C⊗S → Hom_k(S^*,C)) is injective.

Modern reading. This is the standard passage from comodules to 'rational' modules over the dual algebra. The injectivity condition is the Mittag-Leffler / 'α-condition' / local projectivity condition. It is automatic over a field and holds for S projective (or locally projective) over k.
errors: Left/right conventions are loose. With the coaction written C → C⊗S (a right coaction in today's usual convention) and the usual convolution (uv)(s) = Σ u(s₁)v(s₂), the formula u_C = (id⊗u)Δ_C gives a LEFT S^*-module. A right module, as written, requires the opposite convolution or a different coaction convention. This is harmless for the argument.

The injectivity criterion is stated only as giving uniqueness ('on connaît'). It is not stated whether every S^*-module structure (even a 'rational' one) comes from a comodule. That needs C⊗S → Hom(S^*,C) injective plus an image condition; the page leaves this open.

ideas.what: Comodule over a coalgebra S yields a module over the dual convolution algebra S^* = Hom(S,k), with u acting via (id⊗u)∘Δ_C
ideas.where_published: Implicit in the SGA3 Exp. I treatment of linear representations / comodules

ideas.what: A comodule structure is equivalent to a module structure of the functor W(C) = (k' ↦ C⊗k') over the algebra functor V(S) = (k' ↦ Hom(S,k'))
ideas.modern_name: Functorial (Yoneda) description of comodules as modules over the dual vector-group functor
ideas.where_published: SGA3 Exp. I (W(M), V(M) and representations / comodules)

ideas.what: The comodule structure is recoverable from the S^*-module structure when C⊗S → ∏_{u∈S^*} C is injective
ideas.modern_name: α-condition / locally projective (Mittag-Leffler, universally torsionless) coalgebras

deep.surprise_reason: These are textbook-level generalities on comodules versus modules over the dual algebra, including the standard injectivity (α-) condition. The only context of interest is that they are preparation for divided-power coalgebra structures, which the page itself does not develop.
transcription_corrections: 'l'algèbre V_k(k)=S^k' should most likely read 'V_k(S)(k) = S^k': the k-points of the algebra functor V_k(S).
'et OK est bien si' is likely 'et ça va bien si' or 'et (A) est bien si': it is fine provided the map is injective.
Margin insertions 'à g.' / 'à d.' (à gauche / à droite) are correctly placed. The heading 'Généralités sur coalg. et comodules' is boxed at the top right.
